paragraphs.intro: I'm an Electrical Engineer and Software Engineer currently working at Mazda Colombia as a Backend Developer, with a background spanning robotics, embedded systems, signal processing, and software development. I am particularly interested in intelligent physical systems and how perception, computation, and control can be combined to enable robots to operate effectively in the real world.
paragraphs.experience: My engineering experience includes working with autonomous robots, developing tools for fleet monitoring and debugging, designing embedded systems for acoustic sensing, and building software systems across different levels of abstraction. These projects have given me hands-on experience with physical systems as well as the software and computational infrastructure required to operate them.
paragraphs.interests: I am especially interested in robotics, computer vision, and machine learning. I want to explore how robots can perceive and model dynamic environments, anticipate human actions, and use these predictions to make safe and effective decisions when working alongside people.
paragraphs.phd: I am interested in pursuing a PhD where I can explore the intersection of robotics, software, and hardware systems. My interests span intelligent machines, embedded systems, computer vision, circuits and electronics, and cybersecurity, with a particular curiosity for understanding how complex systems can be designed to interact reliably with the physical world.

kiwibot.title: Fleet Control Toolkit
kiwibot.description: Robotics operations, automation, and software infrastructure for an autonomous delivery fleet.

paragraphs.intro: At Kiwibot, I worked as a Service Desk Robotics Engineer supporting an autonomous robotic fleet. My work involved diagnosing failures across both the robots and the software systems surrounding them.
paragraphs.automation: I developed internal tools to automate repetitive debugging and fleet-management workflows, combining telemetry, remote device access, and software diagnostics into reproducible workflows.
paragraphs.debugging: One of these tools was an automated debugging pipeline built in Python. It followed a Trigger → Diagnose → Solution approach, using SSH and robot telemetry to identify and resolve recurring issues. The system reduced more than 50% of incoming service tickets through automation.
paragraphs.infrastructure: I also worked on cloud-based fleet infrastructure, including services deployed through GCP Cloud Run, device-management workflows, and internal APIs. This gave me practical experience with the software infrastructure required to operate autonomous systems at scale.

lambdaEngine.title: Lambda Engine
lambdaEngine.description: A custom C++ game engine developed as a long-term exploration of engine architecture, low-level systems, and software design.

paragraphs.interest: I became interested in game development, but found myself particularly drawn to engine architecture and low-level systems.
paragraphs.engine: Instead of using an existing engine such as Unity or Unreal, I decided to build my own engine in C++. The project became a long-term solo effort focused on understanding system design, abstractions, and design patterns.
paragraphs.sdl: The engine uses SDL2 as its foundation, including SDL2_image, SDL2_mixer, and SDL2_ttf. The work has given me practical experience with memory management, performance considerations, rendering systems, and the organization of larger C++ projects.

mars.title: Marine Acoustic Recording System
mars.description: An embedded platform for underwater acoustic data acquisition, combining custom electronics, real-time firmware, and signal processing.

paragraphs.intro: MARS was developed in the context of underwater acoustics research, combining embedded systems, electronics, and digital signal processing to build a low-cost platform for acoustic experiments.
paragraphs.embedded: I designed and developed the embedded acquisition system around the ESP32, using C, ESP-IDF, and FreeRTOS to manage concurrent acquisition and processing tasks.
paragraphs.analog: The project also involved designing the analog front-end required to interface hydrophone signals with the digital acquisition system. This included signal conditioning, amplification, biasing, and filtering circuits designed and tested using KiCad and LTspice.
paragraphs.signalProcessing: On the software side, I worked with signal-processing techniques including filtering, matched filtering, and spectral analysis, using Python and MATLAB to analyze and validate the acquired data.
paragraphs.evolution: The system evolved from early prototypes into custom PCB designs supporting multi-channel acquisition, providing hands-on experience across the full path from physical sensing and electronics to embedded software and data analysis.
